title: Better disclosure for investors
subject: This guide provides practical principles for listed companies to meet continuous disclosure obligations under the Corporations Law and stock exchange listing rules, aiming to ensure equal access to price-sensitive information for all investors.
background: The guide is issued under the continuous disclosure provisions of the Corporations Law and the ASX Listing Rules. It is intended for directors and executives of listed companies to help them manage disclosure obligations and minimise the risk of breaching the law, while promoting good disclosure practice rather than imposing new regulatory requirements.
ruling: ASIC outlines a set of non-binding principles for better disclosure, emphasising that companies should adopt them flexibly. Key guidance includes: establishing written disclosure policies and procedures; using current technology (e.g., company websites) to disseminate price-sensitive information promptly; nominating a senior officer to oversee and coordinate disclosure; limiting authorised spokespersons; releasing price-sensitive information through the stock exchange before any private briefings; handling rumours and leaks by posting information on the company website; reviewing analyst briefings for inadvertent disclosures; and confining comments on financial projections to factual errors and assumptions. ASIC states that these principles represent good disclosure practice, not regulatory requirements.
legislation_referenced: Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) (formerly Corporations Law) – continuous disclosure provisions
ASX Listing Rules – continuous disclosure requirements
